question: A boutique hotel receives independent walk-in inquiries each afternoon. On a given Tuesday, there are exactly 6 inquiries. Each inquiry independently results in a booking with probability 0.15. What is the probability that at least one booking is made? Give your answer to 3 decimal places.

A two-way interaction plot shows the mean response y on the vertical axis and the levels of factor x (low, high) on the horizontal axis. Two lines represent the levels of factor group (A and B). For group A the line goes from 10 at low to 18 at high. For group B the line goes from 10 at low to 11 at high. What conclusion about the relationship between x and group is supported by this plot?

choices.A: The effect of x on y differs by group because the lines are not parallel
choices.B: There is no interaction because both lines slope upward
choices.C: Group B completely blocks the effect of x because its line is flatter
choices.D: The main effect of group is zero because both lines start at the same height

question: Let x be the date object as.Date('2024-06-15'). Write a one-line R expression that returns the weekday of x as a character string.

In a psychology experiment measuring reaction times, researchers compare a full model (including study method and age) to a reduced model (including only age) using a likelihood ratio test. The software output is shown below.

Likelihood ratio test
data:  full_model and reduced_model
LRT = 7.823, df = 1, p-value = 0.005159

What conclusion does this test support?

choices.A: The full model does not fit significantly better than the reduced model because the p-value is greater than 0.05.
choices.B: The full model fits significantly better than the reduced model because the p-value is less than 0.01.
choices.C: The reduced model is preferred because the likelihood ratio statistic is less than 10.
choices.D: The additional predictors have no effect on reaction time because the degrees of freedom equals 1.

question: When using the nonparametric bootstrap to estimate the bias of a sample statistic T computed from an original dataset, which of the following correctly describes the standard bootstrap bias estimator?

choices.A: The observed statistic minus the mean of the bootstrap replicates, because the bootstrap distribution approximates the true sampling distribution centered at the population parameter.
choices.B: The mean of the bootstrap replicates minus the observed statistic, because the bootstrap replicates are generated from the true underlying population distribution.
choices.C: The mean of the bootstrap replicates minus the observed statistic, because the nonparametric bootstrap treats the empirical distribution of the original sample as the population.
choices.D: The standard deviation of the bootstrap replicates, because bias measures how much the estimator fluctuates across repeated samples.

question: During performance testing of a web application, engineers fit a simple linear regression model with an intercept to predict api_latency from server_load using n test runs. For a particular run, the hat matrix diagonal entry (leverage) is 0.25, and the deleted residual (observed latency minus the prediction from a model fit on all other runs) is 2.4 ms. What is the raw ordinary least squares residual for this run in the full model? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

An agronomist tested three fertilizer formulations on wheat yield (kg per hectare) and ran an analysis of variance followed by a Tukey post-hoc test. The console output for the pairwise comparisons is shown below:

diff       lwr      upr     p adj
Phos-Nit  -12.5   -20.3   -4.7   0.003
K-Nit     -25.8   -33.6  -18.0   < 0.001
K-Phos    -13.3   -21.1   -5.5   0.002

Which statement correctly describes the fertilizer effects on yield?

choices.A: The potassium treatment produced significantly higher yields than both nitrogen and phosphorus treatments.
choices.B: There is no statistically significant difference between any pair of fertilizer treatments at the 0.05 level.
choices.C: The nitrogen treatment produced significantly lower yields than the phosphorus treatment, and the difference between potassium and phosphorus is exactly 25.8 kg per hectare.
choices.D: The nitrogen treatment produced the highest mean yield, and every pair of fertilizers differs significantly at the 0.05 level.

question: An HR analyst compares post-training job satisfaction scores between two groups: employees who attended a leadership workshop (Group T) and those who did not (Group C). The analyst plans a two-sample permutation test on the difference in mean satisfaction scores to test the null hypothesis that the workshop has no effect on mean satisfaction. Suppose the two groups actually have identical mean satisfaction scores, but Group T has a variance three times larger than Group C, and both distributions are non-normal. Which statement correctly describes the validity of the two-sample permutation test under these conditions?

choices.A: The test is invalid because exchangeability under the null requires identical distributions, which is violated by unequal variances.
choices.B: The test remains valid because the null hypothesis concerns only the means, and label permutation automatically balances group variances.
choices.C: The test is invalid because permutation tests strictly require the underlying data to follow a normal distribution.
choices.D: The test remains valid because the central limit theorem ensures the permutation distribution of the mean difference converges to the correct reference.

question: A portfolio manager tracks 5 independent stock trades. Each trade has a 0.30 probability of yielding a positive return. Assuming the outcomes are independent, what is the probability that exactly 2 trades yield a positive return? Give your answer to 3 decimal places.

Consider the following R code.
x <- c(12.3, 55.6, 23.8, 45.1, 91.4, 11.2, 30.0)
x[x >= 40] <- mean(x[x < 40])
sum(x)
What value does this code print? Give your answer to 3 decimal places.

A veterinarian tracks recovery times (in days) for three dog breeds across two clinics. The data is stored in a matrix defined as rec_times <- matrix(c(5, 7, 6, 4, 8, 5), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE), where rows represent clinics and columns represent breeds. Provide a single R expression that calculates the total recovery time for the first clinic.

Given the following summary statistics for a sample of size n = 5: sum(x) = 10, sum(y) = 20, sum(x^2) = 40, sum(y^2) = 100, sum(x*y) = 50. Calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient r. Give your answer to 3 decimal places.

A population is partitioned into K mutually exclusive groups. Sampling procedure X draws a random sample from every group, while procedure Y randomly selects a subset of groups and measures all units within them. Which statement correctly identifies procedure X and the within-group variance structure that makes it most precise for estimating the population mean?

choices.A: X is cluster sampling and is most precise when within-group variance is large
choices.B: X is stratified sampling and is most precise when within-group variance is small
choices.C: X is stratified sampling and is most precise when within-group variance is large
choices.D: X is cluster sampling and is most precise when within-group variance is small

question:
The following output comes from comparing two nested Poisson regression models for monthly mobile data usage (in gigabytes) among subscribers. Model 1 uses only account tenure as a predictor. Model 2 adds a binary indicator for owning a premium router.

Analysis of Deviance Table
Model 1: usage ~ tenure
Model 2: usage ~ tenure + premium_router
Resid. Df Resid. Dev Df Deviance Pr(>Chi)
    1  499     612.40
    2  498     607.59  1   4.8120  0.02826 *

Which statement correctly interprets this likelihood ratio test?

choices.A: The test compares the two models using a t-distribution, and the p-value of 0.028 indicates that tenure alone is a poor predictor of data usage.
choices.B: Because the residual deviance increased in Model 2, the additional router variable degrades the model fit and should be removed.
choices.C: Under the null hypothesis that the router variable has no effect, the deviance difference follows a chi-squared distribution with one degree of freedom, and the significant p-value suggests the full model fits the data better.
choices.D: The test statistic of 4.812 is the estimated coefficient for the router variable, and its significance proves a linear relationship between router quality and data usage.

question: A data frame D contains columns x, y, and z. Column x is a factor. Some rows are duplicates based on columns y and z. To prevent spurious levels from affecting a subsequent glm, you must retain exactly the first occurrence of each unique (y, z) combination and drop all unused factor levels. Write the one-line base R expression that returns the corrected data frame.

A retail analyst records weekly basket sizes and average customer spending.
baskets <- c(2, 4, NA, 5, 3)
spending <- c(15, 30, 25, 35, 18)
model <- lm(spending ~ baskets)
nobs(model)
What does this print?

A graduate teaching assistant models the number of practice problems a student solves until they achieve 4 correct solutions. Each problem is answered independently with probability 0.40 of being correct. Given that a student has already solved 5 problems with only 2 correct, what is the probability that the student will solve at most 6 additional problems to reach the target? Give your answer to 3 decimal places.

A clinical study evaluates a new antihypertensive medication. Among 40 patients who took the drug, 28 showed a reduction in systolic blood pressure of at least 10 mmHg. Calculate the lower bound of the 95% Wilson confidence interval for the true proportion of patients who would experience this reduction. Give your answer to 3 decimal places.
Consider a sequence of random variables X_n and a fixed constant c. If X_n converges in probability to c, which of the following statements is guaranteed to be true?

choices.A: X_n converges almost surely to c.
choices.B: X_n converges in distribution to a non-degenerate random variable.
choices.C: Convergence in probability is a weaker mode of convergence than convergence in distribution.
choices.D: X_n converges in distribution to c.

question: A researcher has fitted two nested Poisson GLMs to model trout counts at water monitoring sites. The reduced model is stored in an object called model_reduced and includes only the predictor ph_level. The full model is stored in model_full and includes both ph_level and a treatment variable. Write the one-line R expression that performs a likelihood-ratio test to compare model_reduced against model_full, explicitly requesting a Chi-squared test statistic.

A researcher runs the following R command on a dataset of survey respondents:
quantile(education_years)
The software prints:
  0%   25%   50%   75%  100%
   6    10    12    16    20
What does the value 12 represent?

choices.A: The median years of education in the sample
choices.B: The mean years of education in the sample
choices.C: The highest years of education in the sample
choices.D: The interquartile range of years of education

question: Consider a two-sample comparison of means between two independent groups with equal sample sizes n per group. Assume the common population standard deviation sigma is 15 and the true difference in means delta is 10. Using the normal approximation formula n = 2 * sigma^2 * (z_0.975 + z_0.90)^2 / delta^2, calculate the required n per group. Give your answer to 3 decimal places.

A two-sided t-test of H0: mu_x = mu_y against Ha: mu_x != mu_y yields a test statistic of t = 2.14 with 98 degrees of freedom and a p-value of 0.035. Which statement correctly describes the meaning of this p-value?

choices.A: The probability that the null hypothesis is true given the observed data.
choices.B: The probability of obtaining a test statistic at least as extreme as the observed value, assuming the null hypothesis is true.
choices.C: The probability that the observed data arose purely from random chance.
choices.D: The probability of making a Type I error in this specific test.

question:
x <- c(1, 2, NA, 4, NA, NA, 7, 8, 9, NA)
sum(is.na(x))
What number does the second line return? Give your answer as a whole number.

A parameter theta follows a Gamma distribution with shape 2 and rate 1. Conditional on theta, random variables X and Y are independent, with X following a Poisson distribution with mean theta and Y following a Poisson distribution with mean 2*theta. Given the observations X = 1 and Y = 2, use Bayes rule to compute the posterior probability that theta exceeds 1. Give your answer to 3 decimal places.
